# Pendo and the Black Mane

Once upon a time, in the heart of the savanna, a lion cub named Pendo lived beside a winding river. His friend Mara was a young tigress with bright stripes and patient paws. Pendo's father, King Kojo, wore a massive black mane that shook when he walked. Everyone in the pride made room for the king.

One morning Pendo watched his father roar at a distant shadow. “Why is Baba so scary?” Pendo asked Mara. Mara tilted her striped head and listened to the rumble fade. “Perhaps you should ask him,” she said.

Pendo crept toward the river while the lionesses went hunting. Mara followed him through the tall grass. A thick fog drifted across the water, and a shooting star flashed above it. For a moment the two friends forgot to be afraid.

Then laughter crackled from the reeds. Three hyenas stepped onto the muddy bank. Pendo tried to roar, but only a tiny squeak escaped. Mara stood beside him and showed her sharp teeth.

A black mane rose behind the grass. King Kojo planted his enormous paws between the friends and the hyenas. “Come here. Now.” His voice rolled across the river. Pendo hurried beneath his father's chest while Mara stayed close. The king swept one paw through the air, and the hyenas fled.

Kojo lowered his scarred nose and gently nudged his cub. “I was frightened too,” he said. Pendo felt his father's breathing slow against his own small back. That evening, Pendo understood that his father's fierce voice could carry love.
